items.title: AFCS · 1 — The control stack
items.description: The AFCS as a stack of layers: which one is holding the aircraft, what it does, what it ignores. SAS, command augmentation, ATT, Wing-Level, and the always-on basic functions.

items.title: AFCS · 2 — Upper modes & the Collective Safety Function
items.description: Armed vs active modes, and the three protections that come with any collective upper mode: power limiting (119/97/145), autorotation protection below 15% torque, and the low-height floors.

items.title: AFCS · 3 — Engagement envelopes & minimum use heights
items.description: Every mode's engagement band and its minimum use height, grouped vertical / transition / longitudinal / hover / lateral / approach, with the absolute rules.

items.title: AFCS · 4 — Coupled approaches
items.description: The four approach-limitation numbers (900/800 fpm, 130 kt profile), the mandatory IAS-mode rule below 50 kt uncoupled, the 7° Cat I ILS certification, and how FMS coupling shows on the PFD.

items.title: AFCS · 5 — Failure logic
items.description: What forces every upper mode off, the four modes built to survive it on purpose, the near-identical AP-malfunction drills, and what comes back to your hands when the layers peel away.

items.title: AFCS · 6 — Cold recap (numbers only)
items.description: Every AFCS number and the fault/survivor sets, no explanation. For the night before a check.

items.title: HTAWS: Managing the Flying Data Center
items.description: How the terrain awareness and warning system thinks, followed through a real terrain event from first alert to resolution.

items.title: Fire: Protection and Emergency Procedures
items.description: How the fire detection and extinguishing system is built, followed through a real engine fire from first indication to a safe outcome.

items.title: Electrical: Failure Logic and Survival
items.description: How the electrical system generates, converts, and distributes power, followed through a real generator failure to show exactly how the system protects itself and what the pilot does.

items.title: Limitations: Operational and Structural Flight Limits
items.description: A complete walkthrough of every operating limitation for the AW169 EP — weight, speed, rotor, engine, and system limits — with a brief note on why each one is set where it is.
